findings.title: The son claim and cosmic unmaking
findings.claim: The focus ties the child claim to a staged cosmic strain: the heavens nearly rupture, the earth splits, and the mountains collapse. Read with the supplied denials and recurrences of the child claim and the account of God originating heaven and earth, the sequence becomes a failure of imposed generation inside an originated order.
findings.mechanism: The supplied analysis of مِنْهُ makes the causal sequence return to the preceding child-claim proposition. In the wider context, 19:35 denies a divine son, 21:26 records the same attribution, and 21:56 names God as the one who originated the heavens and earth. The focus carriers تَكَادُ, يَتَفَطَّرْنَ, تَنشَقُّ, تَخِرُّ, الْجِبَالُ, and هَدًّا contact those claims and the wider cosmic images: 42:5 repeats the near-splitting heavens, 22:31 pictures association with God as a fall from the sky, 73:14 shows earth and mountains shaking, and 69:14 shows them crushed together. This makes the local collapse a cosmic answer to false generation, set against divine origination; the 80:26 connection row nominates a cultivation use of earth-splitting as a counter-reading.
findings.reader_payoff: The catastrophe is more than a free-standing end-time scene: the focus places a claim about divine offspring against the one who originates the heavens and earth, while wider passages reuse the near-splitting, falling, and mountain-collapse images to show the created order under strain.
findings.containment: The focus's causal pronoun is analyzed as resuming the preceding child-claim proposition; the full preceding wording is not included here. The wider passages are contextual parallels, not proof that every cosmic collapse has the same cause. The 80:26 connection nominates earth-splitting for cultivation, but its exact target Arabic supplies only the splitting phrase; this note-level counter-reading keeps the focus's destructive force tied to its causal relation and following collapse rather than to an inherently destructive sense of splitting.

epistemic.reason: The trusted publication anchors the six focus branches, and the focus word alignment is complete. Supplied connection rows provide exact target Arabic but no target morphology or lexical analysis; the represented HFT summary is legacy_unbound and has no exact trace. The interpretation therefore rests on the focus and checkable image/claim contacts, with 80:26 retained as a counter-reading.
